name: application-contact-card
title: Contact Card
description: Compact contact row with an avatar, name, role/company, and quick-action icon buttons (call/email/message) — each action only renders when its handler is provided, so the card never shows a dead button.
useWhen: Showing a person's identity plus one-tap contact actions in a CRM, directory, or team list.
Not every contact has every contact method — the call/email/message buttons should appear conditionally.
A compact single-row layout fits better than a full profile card.
avoidWhen: You need a richer profile (bio, stats, social links) — use a dedicated person hovercard or profile page instead.
The row needs generic trailing content, not specifically call/email/message — use media-object-row instead.
Multiple contacts need to be laid out as a grid of larger cards — use the generic card component instead.
responsiveBehavior: Name and role/company text truncate with ellipsis on narrow widths rather than wrapping, keeping the row a single fixed-height line.
accessibility: Each icon button carries an aria-label naming both the action and the contact (e.g. "Call Priya Shah"), not just the icon alone.
Action buttons are conditionally rendered rather than disabled, so screen readers and keyboard users never encounter a non-functional control.
The avatar uses initials as a text fallback rather than requiring an image.

variants.title: Contact card
variants.description: Single contact row with initials avatar, name, role/company, and call/email/message icon buttons, on a light surface.
accessibility: All three quick-action buttons are shown here to illustrate the full set; omit the corresponding prop to hide any one of them.

variants.title: Contact card (Dark)
variants.description: The same contact row, adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Avatar, text, and icon button colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark backgrounds.
